# Preface {.unnumbered}

## Purpose

Project Intelligence studies one central question:

> How can an embodied agent construct useful internal models of the world,
> reason about possible futures, and safely pursue long-term goals under
> uncertainty?

These notes develop the mathematics, physics, algorithms, and engineering
interpretation needed to investigate that question. They are organised around
autonomous-system capabilities rather than treating mathematics, physics,
robotics, control, and learning as unrelated subjects.

The simulated differential-drive robot is the first experimental platform.
Later phases transfer the resulting ideas to a simulated multirotor UAV.

## How to use this book

Each chapter follows the project lifecycle:

```text
Learn and write -> Engineer -> Verify and release
```

During the learning stage:

1. read one concept and reproduce its notation;
2. work through the derivation without skipping steps;
3. explain the physical or geometric meaning in plain language;
4. complete the short retrieval test without looking at the notes;
5. check the answers or hints and revisit only the missed material;
6. connect the documented model to later requirements, implementation, and
   verification.

Code blocks are display-only unless their opening fence names an executable
Quarto engine such as `{python}`. Display-only examples explain theory without
requiring Jupyter.

## Global conventions

- SI units are used unless a section states otherwise.
- Angles are measured in radians for mathematics and software.
- Vectors are column vectors.
- Coordinate frames are right-handed and orthonormal unless stated otherwise.
- A superscript identifies the frame in which coordinates are expressed, such
  as ${}^{a}\mathbf{v}$.
- A rotation matrix $R_{ab}$ describes the orientation of frame $\{b\}$
  relative to frame $\{a\}$ and maps coordinates from $\{b\}$ to $\{a\}$.
- Equations state their assumptions and units close to where they are used.
- Project notation is defined explicitly before material from different sources
  is combined.

## Source policy

The local [textbook retrieval index](../textbooks/INDEX.md) is the first routing
point for theory. Chapters record the source, chapter or section, and page
convention used. Supplementary material is labelled rather than silently
presented as textbook content.
